thread:
nora: Quick proposal — experiment with a dual-path ingress in the gateway. primary path = low-latency direct to hot pool, fallback path = queued worker pool (longer tail but cheaper). We need to nail semantics for streaming + retries before we wire it up.
sara: high level sounds good. main worry: how do we present a single streaming connection to the client if we switch path mid-request? e.g., partial bytes already sent and then we failover.
liam: cost/ops concern too — double-counting tokens if both paths generate output during a hedged request. we need accounting to avoid billing surprises.
tom: a couple options:
- never switch mid-stream: if primary fails, send final error and let client retry (simpler, but bad UX)
- switch and stitch: gateway keeps an idempotent request/session id and resume token; fallback worker attaches to same session and resumes from last acknowledged token (harder)
- speculative hedging where we suppress client output until we pick the winner (adds latency)
nora: thinking tradeoffs: UX vs correctness vs implementation complexity. Stitching requires a resume contract: client acks byte offsets or token indices that gateway can forward. We already track KV cache positions in runtime; can we expose a minimal resume token from runtime to gateway?
sara: if we require client acks, that changes client API. prefer server-side only solution. maybe gateway can buffer a small tail window (e.g., 2s / 512 tokens) so stitchable output is small.
liam: buffering helps accounting too — if we hold back emitted tokens until commit, only the commit winner is billed. downside: extra tail latency and memory pressure under high concurrency.
ingress-bot: created issue #4621: "dual-path-ingress: resume token contract + billing model" (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4621)
troublesome snippet (proto sketch):
```
message IngressResume {
  string session_id = 1;         // gateway-assigned
  int64 last_ack_token = 2;      // index of last token client acknowledged
  string resume_token = 3;       // opaque runtime cursor
}
```
tom: concrete runtime contract we could try initially:
1) gateway assigns session_id on request accept and streams to client with header X-RW-Session: <id>
2) runtime exposes opaque resume_token periodically (every N tokens or on safe boundaries)
3) on failover, gateway hands resume_token to fallback runtime which reconstructs KV state and resumes at resume_token
4) billing: holding-buffer semantics — gateway buffers last M tokens and only commits billing when runtime confirms output accepted
sara: two implementation followups:
- prototype with M=256 tokens buffer
- feature-flag gated in gateway + runtime
liam: please add metrics we can watch in the prototype: buffered_tokens, resumed_sessions, double_emitted_attempts, buffer_memory_bytes, commit_latency
nora: decision: prototype with stitch-on-resume contract + buffer window = 256 tokens, session_id header + resume_token opaque cursor. if it fails in perf tests, fallback to fail-fast behavior. @tom pls own prototyping plan, @sara pls add API UX note for clients.
tom: will do. plan: gateway patch to add session header + buffer layer, runtime patch to export resume cursor API, e2e test that simulates midstream primary kill and verifies client sees continuous stream (within buffering latency). ETA 2 weeks.
liam: added cost guardrails to the issue: hard cap on buffered memory per-node and circuit breaker for freq resumed sessions.
sara: note: docs + SDKs need a paragraph about possible X-RW-Session header and why clients may see ~200ms tail pause during handoff.
nora: thanks. small todo list in the issue, will sync next Wed 10am. :thumbsup:
